paper_title: BackdoorVLM: A Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Vision-Language Models
reason: BackdoorVLM의 데이터셋 라이선스와 이용 조건(상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포)을 뒷받침하는 근거가 공급된 자료에 없어 게시하지 않습니다. 공식 저장소 카드의 '## LICENSE file' 항목(Apache-2.0)과 본문 문장 'The source code is released under the Apache License 2.0'은 소스 코드에 대한 것입니다. 카드는 'The complete processed dataset will be released separately on Hugging Face'라고 밝힐 뿐 데이터셋의 라이선스를 적지 않았고, 데이터셋 Hugging Face 카드는 공급되지 않았습니다. 코드 라이선스는 데이터셋 라이선스가 아니므로 (a) 형식의 인용으로 쓸 수 없습니다. 또한 LICENSE 파일 항목이 있는 카드는 미표기(absence) 증거가 될 수 없고, 논문 1쪽의 Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 고지는 논문 자체에 대한 것이라 데이터셋에 적용할 수 없습니다. 따라서 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포 네 항목을 증거 없이 채울 수 없습니다. 데이터셋 Hugging Face 카드가 공개되어 공급되거나 저자가 데이터 라이선스를 명시하면 다시 평가할 수 있습니다.

screening.paper_title: BackdoorVLM: A Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Vision-Language Models
screening.abstract: Backdoor attacks undermine the reliability and trustworthiness of machine learning systems by injecting hidden behaviors that can be maliciously activated at inference time. While such threats have been extensively studied in unimodal settings, their impact on multimodal foundation models, particularly vision-language models (VLMs), remains largely underexplored. In this work, we introduce BackdoorVLM, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating backdoor attacks and defenses on VLMs across a broad range of settings. It adopts a unified perspective that injects and analyzes backdoors across core vision-language tasks, including image captioning and visual question answering. BackdoorVLM organizes multimodal backdoor threats into 5 representative categories: targeted refusal, malicious injection, jailbreak, concept substitution, and perceptual hijack. Each category captures a distinct pathway through which an adversary can manipulate a model's behavior. We evaluate these threats using 12 representative attack methods spanning text, image, and bimodal triggers, tested on 2 open-source VLMs and 3 multimodal datasets along with 5 representative defense methods. Our analysis reveals that VLMs exhibit strong sensitivity to textual instructions, and in bimodal backdoors the text trigger typically overwhelms the image trigger when forming the backdoor mapping. Notably, backdoors involving the textual modality remain highly potent, with poisoning rates as low as 1\% yielding over 90\% success across most tasks. Moreover, existing defenses lack generalization across trigger types and backdoor scenarios, leading to unreliable protection against diverse triggers across modalities and forms. These findings highlight significant, underexplored vulnerabilities in current VLMs. We hope that BackdoorVLM can serve as a useful benchmark for analyzing and mitigating multimodal backdoor threats.
